title: Already past four

feedback.title: Avoid another trick, without undoing the extra one
feedback.summary: You are already above target: 5 taken, 4 estimated. Discarding the club loses this trick, but leaves you at five; it cannot restore an exact four.
points: You hold no Hearts, so either card is legal. The club is neither the led suit nor trump and cannot beat the queen of Hearts.
Avoiding another trick is a reasonable local choice, not recovery of the exact target. No scoring benefit is claimed.
Both choices receive Reasonable because exact-target success is already unreachable and no other objective or scoring rule is modeled.

feedback.title: Another win still leaves you above target
feedback.summary: The spade trumps the Hearts and takes a sixth trick. You were already above your estimate of four; winning again cannot recover that exact target.
points: You act last and no other trump has been played, so even the two of Spades wins this trick.
The club would avoid this extra trick, but neither choice can make five already-taken tricks become four.
This rating does not imply a scoring advantage over discarding. Comparing points or other objectives needs rules outside this checkpoint.

author_notes: EC-043 already-above contrast. Equally rated choices intentionally avoid inventing a scoring preference when exact-target success is already impossible. Local loss versus local win is still explicit.
